insights.title: Expert Insights
insights.waves_title: Hunger arrives in waves, not an endless climb
insights.waves_desc: The hunger hormone (ghrelin) peaks during your habitual meal times and naturally subsides within 20 to 30 minutes, even if you do not eat. Sipping warm tea or water helps your body comfortably ride the wave.
insights.autophagy_desc: When digestive work pauses, cells shift energy toward self-clearing mechanisms known as autophagy, breaking down damaged proteins and supporting long-term metabolic health.
insights.circadian_title: Aligning your eating window with daylight
insights.circadian_desc: Insulin sensitivity naturally peaks during morning and afternoon hours. Eating in alignment with daylight rhythms supports healthy blood sugar control and deeper, more restorative sleep.
insights.hydration_desc: As insulin levels drop during a fast, the body naturally releases stored water and sodium. Staying hydrated with water, herbal teas, or a pinch of mineral salt helps prevent afternoon lethargy.
insights.breaking_title: Nourish gently when opening your window
insights.breaking_desc: Breaking your fast with clean proteins, wholesome fats, or cooked vegetables prevents sharp blood sugar spikes and preserves sustained focus and steady afternoon energy.
insights.listen_title: Listening to your body always comes first
insights.listen_desc: Intermittent fasting is a flexible lifestyle practice, never an endurance contest. If you feel dizzy, unwell, or excessively fatigued, end your fast with food. Sustainable consistency always comes before the clock.
insights.switch_title: The gentle shift to metabolic flexibility
insights.switch_desc: After roughly 12 to 14 hours of fasting, liver glycogen stores naturally decrease, encouraging your cells to alternate between glucose and fatty acids for steady, clean cellular energy.
insights.evening_title: Allowing digestion to conclude before bed
insights.evening_desc: Finishing your last meal 2 to 3 hours before sleep allows core body temperature to decrease, promoting deeper slow-wave sleep and natural nighttime recovery.
disclaimer.title: Medical & Scientific Disclaimer
disclaimer.p1: This app is an independent routine tracker created for personal wellness and habit awareness. The insights and scientific studies referenced here are summaries of published academic literature and are provided solely for general educational purposes.
disclaimer.p2: This application does not provide medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment. Intermittent fasting significantly influences metabolic and hormonal functions. Always consult a qualified physician or healthcare provider before beginning or modifying any fasting protocol.
disclaimer.highlight_body: Listen to your body. Fasting should never cause distress or illness. If you experience dizziness, faintness, weakness, or nausea, break your fast immediately with nourishment.
